# Vim App SDK — LLM Context (llms.txt)

> For AI coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, etc.) building on `@vimconnect/app-sdk`.
> The SDK is niche; agents routinely hallucinate methods that don't exist. This
> file is the verified surface for THIS app. When in doubt, read the installed
> types at `node_modules/@vimconnect/app-sdk/dist/index.d.ts` — that is ground
> truth, above any docs page.

## What the SDK is

An in-page client that loads from a CDN and bridges to the Vim Connect Chrome
extension over a MessageChannel. This app runs as an iframe inside the Vim Hub,
injected into a web EHR. One app runs unmodified across many EHRs because the
extension normalizes each into one event/entity model.

## Package facts

- `@vimconnect/app-sdk`, ESM-only. Types at `dist/index.d.ts`.
- Pinned at `0.4.53` in `package.json` — pre-1.0. Re-verify signatures on upgrade.

## One entry point (this app has no Worker)

- **UI app** — `initVimSDK({ accessToken })`. Visible sidebar. Subscribes:
  `sdk.ehr.workflow.on(...)`, `sdk.ehr.context.onChange(...)`.
- This app does not use `initWorkerVimSDK` — `chart_open` already puts the
  provider in front of the open panel, so a Worker would add nothing.

## Auth (OAuth launch flow) — required shape

1. Extension opens the Launch endpoint as `/launch?launch_id=abc123`.
2. Redirect to `{backend}/app-auth/authorize` with: `response_type=code`,
   `client_id`, `launch=abc123`, `scope="launch openid"`,
   `redirect_uri={origin}/app`, `state="abc123:<csrf>"`.
3. Vim redirects to `/app?code=...&state=...`. Validate CSRF from state.
4. The server route POSTs **JSON** (NOT form-urlencoded, NO redirect_uri) to
   `{backend}/app-auth/token`: `{ grant_type:"authorization_code", code,
   client_id, client_secret }`.
5. `initVimSDK({ accessToken })` → `sdk.hub.setActivationStatus("ENABLED")`.
- Backend host is `api.getvim.ai` (prod) / `api.stage.getvim.ai` (staging).
- Auth codes are single-use; there is no refresh flow. Expiry → re-launch from
  the Hub.
- `CLIENT_SECRET` is server-only. Only `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` reaches the browser.

## Reads used by this app

- `sdk.ehr.workflow.on('chart_open', ...)` → bare id reference, one-shot.
- `sdk.ehr.context.onChange('chart_open:patient' | 'encounter_open:patient', ...)`
  → `curr.fields`, used only as a fallback signal that a patient is in view.
- `sdk.ehr.api.patient.getPatient()` → `ApiResponse<Patient>` (no-arg — resolves
  from current context).
- `sdk.ehr.api.patient.getProblems()` → `ApiResponse<Diagnosis[]>` (no-arg).
- `sdk.ehr.context.onChange('encounter_open:encounter', ...)` → `curr.fields`
  (current visit only — no history list exists).
- `sdk.ehr.workflow.on('order_select', ...)` → bare id reference, one-shot, then
  `sdk.ehr.api.order.getOrderById()` (no-arg) for whatever single order is in
  context. **No CPT/procedure code field. No status field** (open/closed).
- `sdk.ehr.context.onChange('referral_start:referral', ...)` → `curr.fields`.
  **There is no `sdk.ehr.api.referral` namespace** — this context key is the
  only source.
- A method existing in the `.d.ts` does NOT guarantee it's implemented in a
  given EHR build — every Entity API call here is wrapped in retry-with-backoff
  (`src/lib/retry.ts`) and treats `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` as `unsupported`, not `error`.

## Writeback

None. This app has no writeback ceremony anywhere — it is read-only by design.

## What does NOT exist (do not invent)

- **No patient-visit-history API** — only the current encounter is readable.
- **No bulk open-orders list** — only whatever single order happens to be in
  context via `order_select`.
- **No care-team entity** — "other providers referenced" is derived from
  whatever provider name fields are attached to an in-context order/referral,
  never a full roster.
- **No order status field** — do not infer open/closed from name/reason text.
- **No insights/gaps API.**
- **No `sdk.ehr.api.referral` namespace** (only patient/encounter/order are
  declared). For referral data, subscribe to the `referral_start:referral`
  context key.

## Framework notes (Next.js App Router)

- `useSearchParams()` requires a `<Suspense>` wrapper.
- Guard init/redirect effects with a `useRef` so React StrictMode doesn't
  double-fire.
- Port is not fixed by Vim — it must match your registered App URL and redirect
  URI. Keep the running port, registered URLs, and redirect URI consistent.
